summary: I read all 367 sohzm/cheating-daddy issues (title, body and every comment, dumped with `gh issue list --state all --json ...,comments`) and the 116 PRs. About 75 issues are Windows-related or are "doesn't work at all" reports that a Windows user could have filed. Most of the reported "not working on Windows" traffic has nothing to do with Windows. It comes from Gemini model and API churn: the Live model was shut down on 2025-12-09, `enableSpeakerDiarization` was rejected, gemini-2.5-flash and gemma-3-27b-it returned 404 for new keys, and `googleSearch`/`proactivity` closed every Live session. That covers #168 (41 comments), #176, #318, #452 and #339, plus about 30 other issues. The fork already avoids all of it: gemini-3.8-live, gemini-3.8-flash, no proactivity, and Google Search off by default. Since the fork works on macOS with the same code and key, this pattern cannot explain a Windows-only failure. Six Windows-specific patterns remain: (1) no system audio on Windows (#161, three PCs, plus #117, #126, #207, #462); (2) getDisplayMedia/desktopCapturer failures on multi-monitor or multi-GPU machines, which show as "error" status and dead screenshot hotkeys (#198, #172 log); (3) local-AI Whisper crashing the whole process on Windows because of `device: 'auto'` (#239, #421, #373); (4) Squirrel Setup.exe install failures and people editing source that the installed app never loads (#422, #206, #165, #352, #368, #383); (5) stealth problems (taskbar, process name, tooltips shown in screen share); (6) zoom stuck and hotkeys. Fork status: the model, Google Search and taskbar fixes are present. The screenshot path is rewritten to main-process desktopCapturer, which partly fixes pattern 2. The PR #298 fixes are missing: `.catch`/empty-source guard on `setDisplayMediaRequestHandler` and `device:'cpu'`. Separately, the fork itself added a Windows-only audio path that macOS never runs. With the default audioMode `speaker_only`, Windows sends loopback audio through a new AudioWorklet (renderer.js:709-731), while macOS uses SystemAudioDump and never creates the worklet (renderer.js:703-707). Any error in that path, or a getDisplayMedia call that never returns, ends or hangs the whole meeting start (renderer.js:740-742, CheatingDaddyApp.js:703-704, sessionController.js:43-52). Upstream issues are the only evidence for that path, so the Mac session working says nothing about it.

issues.title: Windows 11 – Live session connected, "message sent", but stuck on "Hey, I'm listening to your job interview?"
issues.symptom: Session shows 'Live session connected' and the timer runs, but no answer ever appears and there is no error. 41 comments, mostly 'same here'; one reports the same on macOS.
issues.rootCause: Google shut down gemini-live-2.5-flash-preview on 2025-12-09. After a fix, the next error was `Invalid JSON payload received. Unknown name "enableSpeakerDiarization" at 'setup.input_audio_transcription'`, and the free tier had zero Live quota. Not Windows-specific.
issues.fixReference: Upstream 0.5.0 release (2025-12-12), PR #186 (closed, not merged), later upstream 998a056 (#385) and v0.8.0
issues.evidence: Fork uses `GEMINI_LIVE_MODEL = 'gemini-3.8-live'` (src/utils/gemini.js:66); Live config has no diarization or proactivity (src/utils/geminiLiveSessionConfig.js:29-60); BYOK Live works on Mac.

issues.title: Cheating daddy is not working in any windows device
issues.symptom: 'unable to use the api key and respond' on every Windows device
issues.rootCause: Comments blame free-tier quota cuts (gemini-2.5-flash about 20 RPD; 2.5 Pro removed) and the Live model deprecation of the same week. Nobody identified a Windows-specific cause; reported 2025-12-14, five days after the Live model shutdown.
issues.evidence: Same as #168: fork model ids gemini.js:66, analyzeScreenSend.js:59.

issues.title: Windows: Application does not detect audio (no microphone/speaker selection)
issues.symptom: App starts but captures no audio on any of three Windows PCs; no device picker
issues.rootCause: Never diagnosed by the maintainer. Upstream's Windows path calls getDisplayMedia with `audio:'loopback'` and enables echoCancellation, noiseSuppression and autoGainControl on the loopback track (upstream/master src/utils/renderer.js:315-329). It has no try/catch fallback, and loopback only records the default output device. PR #186 turned AEC/NS/AGC off for loopback and added a mic fallback; PR #164 and #212 added device selection.
issues.fixReference: PR #164 (device selection, closed), PR #186 (AEC off + fallbacks, closed), PR #212 (mic permission/device, closed). None merged.
issues.evidence: Fork's new path disables AEC/NS/AGC on loopback (src/utils/renderer.js:633-643) and treats a getDisplayMedia failure as a warning (renderer.js:709-716). It has no device selection and routes Windows audio through a new AudioWorklet that macOS never runs (renderer.js:650-652, 703-731).

issues.title: screenshot hotkeys not working, overlay shows "error"
issues.installMethod: Both the GitHub source build and the Windows installer
issues.symptom: Screenshots never work; only the word 'error' shows in the top-right. Changing hotkeys, disabling the second monitor and regenerating the key did not help.
issues.rootCause: In that version, startCapture's catch sets status 'error' when Windows `getDisplayMedia` rejects; there was no fallback, so mediaStream stayed null and screenshots returned early. PR #298 reports the same failure on Windows multi-GPU/multi-adapter machines: a DOMException from DXGI enumeration. It added `.catch(()=>callback({}))`, `useSystemPicker:false`, a desktopCapturer/getUserMedia fallback and `disable-gpu-sandbox`.
issues.fixReference: PR #298 (closed, not merged); PR #431/#279 display selection (closed)
issues.evidence: Fork screenshots no longer need getDisplayMedia: IPC 'capture-screen-still' runs desktopCapturer in main (renderer.js:508, screenStill.js:72-90). setDisplayMediaRequestHandler still lacks .catch or an empty-sources guard and still uses useSystemPicker:true (src/utils/window.js:149-156), and there is no disable-gpu-sandbox (index.js:17-19 only disables CalculateNativeWinOcclusion).

findings.title: Windows-only AudioWorklet capture path; any failure in it aborts the whole meeting, and the Mac never runs it
evidence: src/utils/renderer.js:703-707 @8c49d85 – macOS with the default audioMode only calls ipc 'start-macos-audio' (SystemAudioDump); no browser stream
src/utils/renderer.js:709-716 – on non-macOS, getLoopbackStream() (getDisplayMedia) feeds mediaStream
src/utils/renderer.js:728-731 – setupSharedAudioWorklet runs only when a browser stream exists, so on Windows speaker_only it always runs and on Mac speaker_only it never does
src/utils/renderer.js:650-652 – `new AudioContext({sampleRate})` + `audioWorklet.addModule(new URL('./audio-worklet.js', window.location.href).href)` (file inside app.asar when packaged)
src/utils/renderer.js:740-742 – any throw → stopCapture() and `{success:false}`
src/components/app/CheatingDaddyApp.js:703-704 – `if (!capture.success) throw new Error(capture.error || 'Audio capture failed')`
src/utils/sessionController.js:43,50-52 – a startCapture failure runs cleanup(), which stops the provider (the Gemini session) too
src/storage.js:27 – default audioMode 'speaker_only'
Upstream #161 (3 Windows PCs, no audio) shows Windows audio capture was already the weakest path upstream
findings.explanation: On macOS the fork never builds the worklet in its default mode, so the Mac session working proves nothing about this path. On Windows every meeting builds the worklet: an AudioContext at 16000 or 24000 Hz, addModule loading src/audio-worklet.js through a file:// URL inside app.asar, and a ChannelMerger fed by the 48 kHz stereo loopback track. If any step rejects (addModule fetch, AudioWorkletNode construction, audioContext.resume), startCapture returns success:false. CheatingDaddyApp then throws 'Audio capture failed' and SessionController tears down the Live session. To the user, nothing works on Windows: the session starts and stops at once, or shows an error. Whether one of these steps actually fails on Windows is unverified [INFERENCE]. The structural risk, and the fact that the Mac never exercises it, are confirmed by the code. Upstream used ScriptProcessor for Windows, so upstream issues say nothing about this path.
findings.fix: Make worklet failures non-fatal: catch around setupSharedAudioWorklet and fall back to text and Analyze Screen with an 'audio unavailable' status, as is already done when inputs is empty. Log the actual error to the transport log. Test on Windows, or on Mac with audioMode 'both' so the worklet path runs. Consider loading the worklet from a Blob or data URL to avoid a file:// fetch from asar.

findings.title: setDisplayMediaRequestHandler has no catch or empty-source guard; on Windows getDisplayMedia can stay pending forever and the meeting never starts
evidence: src/utils/window.js:149-156 @8c49d85 – `desktopCapturer.getSources({types:['screen']}).then(sources => { callback({ video: sources[0], audio: 'loopback' }); });` with no .catch and no sources.length check, `{ useSystemPicker: true }`
src/utils/renderer.js:709-716 – startCapture awaits getLoopbackStream() on every non-macOS start; a pending promise is never caught
Upstream #172 log: 'UnhandledPromiseRejectionWarning: Failed to get sources.' (https://github.com/sohzm/cheating-daddy/issues/172)
Upstream #198: Windows, two monitors, status 'error', screenshots dead in both the installer and source builds (https://github.com/sohzm/cheating-daddy/issues/198)

PR #298 (closed): Windows 11 multi-GPU, getDisplayMedia DOMException from DXGI enumeration; fix `.catch(() => callback({}))`, empty-sources → callback({}), useSystemPicker:false, disable-gpu-sandbox (https://github.com/sohzm/cheating-daddy/pull/298)
src/index.js:17-19 – the only win32 switch is disable-features=CalculateNativeWinOcclusion
findings.explanation: macOS never calls getDisplayMedia in the fork (renderer.js:703-709), so this handler only runs on Windows and Linux. If desktopCapturer.getSources rejects (a known failure on multi-GPU or multi-adapter Windows machines per PR #298 and #172), callback is never called. Electron's getDisplayMedia promise then neither resolves nor rejects, so startCapture never returns and SessionController stays in 'starting' with no error shown. If getSources returns an empty array, callback({video: undefined, audio: 'loopback'}) is passed an invalid source. The fork's try/catch at renderer.js:710-716 only handles rejection, not a hang.
findings.fix: Port PR #298's handler: `.then(sources => sources.length ? callback({ video: sources[0], audio: 'loopback' }) : callback({})).catch(() => callback({}))`. Add a timeout race around getLoopbackStream. Optionally add `app.commandLine.appendSwitch('disable-gpu-sandbox')` on win32, as PR #298 did.

findings.title: Local AI on Windows crashes the whole Electron process (Whisper device:'auto' → DirectML)
evidence: src/utils/localai.js:181-185 @8c49d85 – `pipeline('automatic-speech-recognition', modelName, { dtype: 'q8', device: 'auto' })`
Upstream #239 (Win11 dual GPU, instant close, single-instance lock held), #421 (Win11 RTX 4050, app exits on Start Session), #373 (Windows, crash after model load)
PR #298 and PR #434 change it to device:'cpu' and add ONNX cache-corruption recovery (https://github.com/sohzm/cheating-daddy/pull/434)
Upstream 800df4d (v0.8.0) removed transformers.js and added src/utils/native-ai-runtime.js
findings.explanation: On Windows, onnxruntime-node with device 'auto' tries DirectML, and on some GPUs that crashes natively, outside any try/catch. On macOS it uses CPU or CoreML, so a Mac test of Local AI succeeds. Only relevant if the Windows user chose Local AI mode rather than BYOK.
findings.fix: Use device:'cpu' (make DirectML opt-in). Catch 'Protobuf parsing failed', delete the model cache and retry once (PR #434).

findings.title: Gemini model/config churn behind most 'not working on Windows' upstream reports is already fixed in the fork
evidence: src/utils/gemini.js:66 – GEMINI_LIVE_MODEL = 'gemini-3.8-live'
src/utils/analyzeScreenSend.js:59 – 'gemini-3.8-flash'
src/storage.js:30 – googleSearchEnabled:false; src/utils/gemini.js:643-650 adds googleSearch only when enabled
src/utils/geminiLiveSessionConfig.js:29-60 – no proactivity, no enableSpeakerDiarization

Leftovers: src/utils/gemini.js:933 'gemma-3-27b-it' (reachable only via dispatchTranscription; resetTranscriptionSilenceTimer at :990 has no callers); src/storage.js:391-403 getAvailableModel returns 'gemini-2.5-flash' (no callers in src)
findings.explanation: #168, #176, #318 and #452 are the issues titled or reported as 'not working on Windows'. Their root causes are server-side model and schema changes that hit every OS. The fork uses current models and drops the fields that close the session, and the same BYOK session works on Mac. So these do not explain the fork's Windows-only failure.

findings.title: Windows install path is riskier in the fork than upstream: native deps and a git+ssh lockfile entry; upstream install-failure reports carry no diagnostics
evidence: package.json:36-40,59 @8c49d85 – @huggingface/transformers (onnxruntime-node, sharp), uiohook-napi, ollama, optional @img/sharp-win32-x64; upstream/master package.json deps are only @google/genai, electron-squirrel-startup, ws
package-lock.json:695 – @electron/node-gyp resolved as git+ssh://git@github.com/electron/node-gyp.git (upstream lockfile has the same at line 664)
forge.config.js:6-8 – asar unpack list for native modules

Upstream #422 (0.7.0 Setup.exe 'Installation has failed', screenshot), #206 (log is from Flow Launcher, no Cheating Daddy data), #383 (Windows commenter: Electron install error), #368/#352 (edits not taking effect in the installed asar)
findings.explanation: Upstream issues show Windows install failures but no root causes. Compared with upstream v0.8.0, the fork adds native modules that need Windows binaries for Electron 44's ABI. A Windows `npm install` that cannot fetch git+ssh dependencies, prebuilt binaries, or the lazily downloaded Electron fails before the app starts [INFERENCE]. Also, Windows users who edit source and then run an older Setup.exe build will not see their changes (asar + OnlyLoadAppFromAsar fuse, forge.config.js:74-75).
findings.fix: Ask the user for the exact Windows error at install or launch. Build the .exe on Windows (or in CI on windows-latest) with `npm ci && npm run make`. Rewrite the lockfile's git+ssh resolved URL to git+https.
